about:
# LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown This is an implementation of Markdown that produces HTML suitable for *World of Warcraft*'s `SimpleHTML`, which supports only a very limited number of HTML tags. LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown is a fork of [LibMarkdown-1.0](https://github.com/endurantgames/WoW-LibMarkdown) by Oraibi-MoonGuard, which is no longer maintained. It registers under its own LibStub name, `LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown-1.0`, so it never collides with copies of LibMarkdown that other AddOns still embed. See [Changes from LibMarkdown](#changes-from-libmarkdown). LibMarkdown (and thus LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown) is heavily based on the [Lua markdown library](https://github.com/mpeterv/markdown) created by Niklas Frykholm and further developed by Peter Melnichenko. All versions of this code are released under the **MIT License**, including this library. ## Why Markdown? Simply put, markdown is easier to read, write, and edit than HTML, and that simplicity makes it easier to produce clean-looking HTML in `SimpleHTML` frames. For example, documentation blocks in code can be created quickly and easily, without having to worry that you forgot to close the right tags. ## Usage The library's main function is `:ToHTML()` (also available as `:ToHtml()`), which takes either a single string or a table of strings (joined as lines), and returns a string with HTML formatting, appropriate for the `:SetText()` function on a `SimpleHTML` frame. An optional second argument changes the [configuration](#configuration) for that call only. ``` local LSHM = LibStub("LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown-1.0"); local MyFrame = CreateFrame("SimpleHTML"); local text = { "# LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown", "", "This is an implementation of Markdown that produces HTML suitable for", "*World of Warcraft*'s **SimpleHTML**, which supports only a very limited", "number of HTML tags." }; MyFrame:SetText( LSHM:ToHTML(text) ); ``` ## Installation Load this library as you normally would -- include `LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown.xml` in your AddOn's TOC or XML file. You are probably already using `LibStub`, but if you aren't, there's a copy included with this AddOn; load `LibStub\LibStub.lua` before the library. The XML also loads an optional AceGUI widget (`SimpleHTMLMarkdown_Description`). It only registers when `AceGUI-3.0` is already loaded, so AddOns that don't use Ace3 can embed the library as-is. ## Markdown Support LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown supports the following parts of [standard markdown](https://commonmark.org/help/), with some extensions. ``` # Heading 1 ## Heading 2 ### Heading 3 Heading 1 ========= Heading 2 --------- ``` These are rendered as `<h1>`, `<h2>`, and `<h3>` HTML tags. As in CommonMark, the `#`s must be followed by a space, so `#hashtag` stays text. `SimpleHTML` has no smaller heading styles and no inline font sizes, so `####` to `######` headings are lines at text size, set apart by color as GitHub does: level 4 in the `strong` color, level 5 in the `strong_em` color, and level 6 in gray. Each level has `h4`, `/h4`, and `h4_style` settings (and so on); `h4_style` names the setting whose color the heading takes. To show level 4 as `<h3>` instead: `h4 = "

"`, `["/h4"] = "


"`, `h4_style = false`. ``` [Link Name](http://LinkURL) [Link Name][1] [Link Name][2] [3] [1]: http://LinkURL [2]: mailto:user@example.org [3]: http://LinkURL ``` Hyperlinks are rendered as you'd expect; however, please note that you need to explicitly define handlers for hyperlinks on your `SimpleHTML` frame for the links to be anything except cosmetic. Note that your handler can be written to process whatever type of links you define; e.g., some of our code has links of the type `[Color Settings](setting:colors)` or `[Color Help](help:colors)`. ``` * List One Item + List One Item - List One Item ^ - List Two Item + List Two Item * List Two Item ``` `SimpleHTML` does not support `<ul>` lists. However, LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown has rudimentary support for lists, presenting them as separate paragraphs with a marker before each. If you have consecutive lists, use a caret (`^`) alone on a line to indicate the end of the current list. The caret isn't shown. ``` 1. List Item 2) List Item 3. List Item ^ a) List Item B. List Item c) List Item ^ i] List Item II. List Item iii] List Item iv. List Item ``` Likewise, LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown will generate pseudo-ordered lists, even though `SimpleHTML` doesn't support `<ol>`. As an extension to standard markdown, LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown supports letters or Roman numerals for lists. (To distinguish between Roman numeral one and a lowercase I, use a square bracket for `i]`.) A letter or Roman numeral list needs at least two items in sequence, so a line like "A. Lincoln was president." stays text. ``` - Fruit - Apple - Granny Smith - [ ] Not done yet - [x] Done ``` Indent an item at least two spaces past its parent's marker to nest it. Each level is indented further (the `list_indent` setting), and `list_marker_2`, `list_marker_3`, and so on can set a different marker per level. Task list items (GitHub's `[ ]` and `[x]`) show an empty box or a check mark in place of the marker. ``` | Spell | Cost | |-----------|-----:| | Fireball | 2% | | Frostbolt | 1% | ``` `SimpleHTML` can't lay out columns, so a table is shown one row per line, with the cells between dim `|` separators and the header row in its own color. A table is centered or right-aligned when every one of its columns is. Use `\|` for a pipe inside a cell. ``` > A blockquote. > > > A quote inside it. ``` A blockquote is shown in gray with a bar at the start of each line (`blockquote_bar`), and a quote inside a quote adds a second bar. `SimpleHTML` can't put the bar on the wrapped part of a long line; `SetIndentedWordWrap` on your frame indents those parts instead. ``` ~~Strikethrough~~ https://example.org and www.example.org ``` `SimpleHTML` can't draw a line through text, so strikethrough is shown dimmed. Bare `http://`, `https://`, and `www.` addresses become links, like ``. ``` Arcane Blast stacks four times.[^stacks] [^stacks]: The stacks end 18 seconds after the first cast, or when you cast Arcane Barrage. ``` A footnote reference shows as a number, `[1]`, numbered in the order the text first refers to it. The notes are listed after a rule at the end of the document. A note can go on in lines indented under it. ### Extensions from other Markdown flavors None of these are in CommonMark or the GFM spec, but each is the syntax other renderers use: ``` > [!NOTE] > GitHub's alerts: [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING], and [!CAUTION]. Term : A definition (PHP Markdown Extra, Pandoc) ==Highlighted==, x^2^, and H~2~O (Pandoc, markdown-it) ## Setup {#setup} [Jump to setup](#setup) ``` - An alert is shown as its kind's icon and title, then its text. The titles are config keys (`admonition_note` and so on), so they can be translated. - A definition list shows each term in its own color, with its definitions indented under it. - `SimpleHTML` can't color a background, so highlighted text is colored instead. - Superscripts and subscripts use the Unicode characters for digits, `+ - = ( )`, and (in a superscript) `n` and `i`. Anything else is shown dimmed. Set `script_glyphs` to `false` to always dim them. - A heading's `{#id}` isn't shown. `SimpleHTML` can't scroll to a heading, so a `[link](#id)` is handed to your hyperlink handler as `#id`. `:GetHeadings(text)` lists a document's headings (`level`, `text`, and `id`, which is the `{#id}` or a GitHub-style id from the text), for a table of contents or for acting on those links. ### WoW extensions ``` ![](atlas:groupfinder-icon-role-large-tank) ![](atlas:groupfinder-icon-role-large-tank 32x32) :check: :x: :question: :warning: :gold: :silver: :copper: :tank: :healer: :dps: [Fireball](spell:133) [Hearthstone](item:6948) [Level 10](achievement:6) ``` - An `atlas:` image is an atlas, shown inside the line (`` only takes texture files). Without a size it's as tall as the text. - A `spell:`, `item:`, `currency:`, or `achievement:` image is that thing's icon, looked up when the text is rendered and shown inside the line: `![](spell:133)`. An unknown id shows a question mark. - A texture marked `inline`, `![](Interface\\ICONS\\X 16x16 inline)`, is shown inside the line too. Without `inline`, an image is a block of its own, as below. - A `:shortcode:` with a config entry under that key is replaced by it. Add your own, such as `[":myicon:"] = "|TInterface\\ICONS\\X:0|t"`. Unknown shortcodes are shown as typed, and `\:check:` is shown as `:check:`. - Game links are ordinary links. To show the game's tooltip for `spell:`, `item:`, `currency:`, and `achievement:` links, use the library's helpers in your frame's hyperlink scripts: ``` html:SetScript("OnHyperlinkEnter", function(self, link) LSHM:ShowLinkTooltip(self, link) end) html:SetScript("OnHyperlinkLeave", function() LSHM:HideLinkTooltip() end) ``` ``` ![Alt Text](Interface\\ICONS\\ABILITY_SAP.PNG) ![Alt Text](Interface\\ICONS\\ABILITY_SAP.PNG "Sap Icon" 64x64 right) ``` This will produce an '<img>' tag, referencing an in-game texture. As an extension to standard markdown, a caption, the desired image dimensions, and an alignment can be specified. These must all be separated from each other and the texture's path by spaces. Acceptable values for alignment are `right`, `left`, and `center`. Dimensions must be specified as a consecutive pair -- width/height -- but a number of formats are acceptable: ``` ![Alt Text](Interface\\ICONS\\ABILITY_SAP.PNG 64x64) ![Alt Text](Interface\\ICONS\\ABILITY_SAP.PNG 64/64) ![Alt Text](Interface\\ICONS\\ABILITY_SAP.PNG 64:64) ![Alt Text](Interface\\ICONS\\ABILITY_SAP.PNG 64,64) ![Alt Text](Interface\\ICONS\\ABILITY_SAP.PNG 64 64) ``` ### HTML Entities `SimpleHTML` only recognizes the following HTML character entities: ``` & ampersand & " double-quote " < less than < > greater than > ``` In addition, the following entities are implemented in LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown: ```   About the the size of a normal space, but non-breaking.   The size of the font itself, so a square.   1/2 the size of the font. &em13; 1/3 of the font size. &em14; 1/4 of the font size.   1/5 of the font size; non-breaking. ``` Numeric references (`©`, `—`) and common named ones (Latin-1 letters and symbols, dashes, curly quotes, `…`, arrows, and so on) are converted to the character itself. Any other entity is shown literally. WoW's fonts may not have a glyph for every character. ### WoW Raid Targeting Icons You can use these in your markdown: ``` {Triangle}, {diamond}, {rt4}, etc ``` ### Partial Support Due to the limitations of `SimpleHTML`, these have limited support. ``` *Italicized Text* _Italicized Text_ **Bold Text** __Bold Text__ ``` `SimpleHTML` has no ability to produce inline bolding or italics, and doesn't recognize `<b>`, `<i>`, `<em>`, or `<strong<` HTML tags. An `_` between two letters or digits is literal, so `snake_case_names` aren't emphasized. See below under "Configuration", however. ``` local hello = { world = "This is a code block." } print(hello.world) ``` ``` print("Code blocks can also be created by starting a line with 4 spaces.") ``` Fences can also be `~~~`, or four or more backticks to hold a line of three. A `|` in code is shown as itself rather than starting a UI escape sequence. ## Configuration LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown requires no specific configuration to use, and usually the default options will work just fine. However, you are able to change the appearance of certain unsupported tags -- specificially the colors -- by embedding UI escape codes. The library object is shared by every AddOn that embeds it, so don't change its `config` table: your settings would apply to every other AddOn's text too. Instead, pass your settings to `:ToHTML()`, which applies them to that call only: ``` local LSHM = LibStub("LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown-1.0"); local settings = { ["em"] = "|cffbbbb00", -- emphasized text in yellow ["/em"] = "|r", -- this ends the yellow text; close your tags! ["list_marker"] = "|TInterface\\MINIMAP\\TempleofKotmogu_ball_purple.PNG:0|t", -- a purple ball for the list marker }; MyFrame:SetText( LSHM:ToHTML(text, settings) ); ``` Or make a renderer of your own with `:New()`. It uses your settings, and the library's defaults for anything you leave out, and keeps working when a newer copy of the library loads: ``` local MyMarkdown = LibStub("LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown-1.0"):New(settings); MyFrame:SetText( MyMarkdown:ToHTML(text) ); ``` AddOns that do change the shared `config` keep their changes when a newer copy of the library loads. Besides the tags and colors, one setting changes how text is read: `hard_breaks`. Set it to `true` for text people type as they would in chat, such as notes: every line break in a paragraph is shown, and a blank line after a paragraph is an empty line, as in a GitHub comment. By default, as in Markdown, lines join into one paragraph unless one ends with two spaces or a backslash, and paragraphs are stacked without a gap. The library keeps its 20 most recent renders, by text and settings, so showing a document again doesn't render it again. Changing any setting, in any of these ways, renders it anew. To see what you can change, see the source or type `/script LibStub("LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown-1.0"):ShowConfig()` ## Demo Frames Included in this package is a `Demo.lua` file that you can enable in `LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown.xml`. It has some sample code; to view it once it's loaded, type `/script LSHMDemoFrame:Show()`. `Showcase.lua`, also enabled in `LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown.xml`, is a page-by-page tour of everything the library renders, for checking a change by eye in game. Each case shows its markdown, what you should see, and the result. Type `/lshm` to open it. ## Errors If rendering ever fails, `:ToHTML()` doesn't raise the error into your code. It reports it through WoW's error handler (so BugSack and the like show it) and returns the text as plain paragraphs, so your frame still shows something readable. Set `raise_errors` on the library to get the error itself while developing. ## Tests `tests/run_tests.py` renders the showcase cases, the demo text, a set of probes, and some real AddOn news pages under Lua 5.1, and checks that each output is markup `SimpleHTML` can parse and matches its golden file in `tests/golden/`. It needs [lupa](https://pypi.org/project/lupa/) (`pip install lupa`). After an intended change to the output, run it with `--update` and review the golden file diffs. It also renders a few hundred random documents built from every syntax the library knows, valid and malformed, and checks that each one renders to markup `SimpleHTML` can parse; set `FUZZ_SEED` and `FUZZ_COUNT` to try others. GitHub Actions runs the tests on every push, and before each release. `Demo.lua` and `Showcase.lua` are for development. Enable them in `LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown.xml` locally, but commit them commented out: `tests/check_release_files.py` fails the push's tests, and stops a release tag from being packaged, if the TOC or an XML file it loads would load one. ## Changes from LibMarkdown LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown 1.0 minor 1 starts from LibMarkdown-1.0 minor 9, the last version on [GitHub](https://github.com/endurantgames/WoW-LibMarkdown) (CurseForge's last file is minor 7). ### Renamed - The library registers as `LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown-1.0`, starting again at minor 1. - The files are `LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown.lua`, `.xml`, and `.toc`. - The AceGUI widget type is `SimpleHTMLMarkdown_Description`; its globals are `LIBSIMPLEHTMLMARKDOWN_WIDGET_CONFIG` and `LIBSIMPLEHTMLMARKDOWN_WIDGET_LINKHANDLER_POPUP`; its methods and config key are `GetLibSimpleHTMLMarkdown`, `SetLibSimpleHTMLMarkdownConfig`, and `LibSimpleHTMLMarkdownConfig`. - The demo frame is `LSHMDemoFrame`. - LibMarkdown's unfinished `SimpleMarkdown.lua` rewrite was never loaded and is not included. ### Fixed - Loading a copy no newer than one already loaded no longer errors. - `:ToHTML()` accepts a table of strings, as documented; it previously always printed an error. A table with a non-string item is now rejected instead of erroring inside the parser. - Roman numeral lists (`i.`, `ii.`) are typed as roman numerals. - A code fence on the last line no longer errors. - `` autolinks no longer call an undefined `encode_email_address`. - Reference links and images no longer index a missing `link_database`. - Empty text passed through tab expansion or code encoding returns `""` instead of erroring. - Blank lines inside a blockquote put a non-breaking space between their line breaks. - An unclosed code fence no longer turns later documents into code blocks. The fence state was kept on the library object, which every AddOn shares. - A `<` that doesn't start a tag (`x`. HTML inside a code fence stays code. - Blocks are never nested, since SimpleHTML can't lay them out. Loose list items, code in list items, and headings or images inside another block become a flat run of blocks. - Character references SimpleHTML can't parse are decoded (see [HTML Entities](#html-entities)). `©` was shown as `©`, and `©` reached SimpleHTML undecoded. - The AceGUI widget only registers when `AceGUI-3.0` is loaded, keeps its library reference (it was overwritten with `false`), and its default list marker uses the `list_marker` key the library actually reads. - The AceGUI widget's settings apply to its own text; they were written into the library's shared config, changing every AddOn's text. - A closing tag with no opening tag (``) is dropped, a tag left open is closed with its block, and `
`, ``, and `
` are self-closed, since SimpleHTML can't parse them otherwise. - Blockquote lines are joined with a space instead of run together, and a blank `>` line no longer adds a stray `"`. - `_` inside a word, `#hashtag`, and `**x**` (one character) are rendered as CommonMark does. - A `|` in code no longer starts a UI escape sequence. - The `^` that ends a list isn't shown, and a list right after it is still a list. - Lists nest, list items are numbered from their own lines, and an item's indented paragraphs and code stay in the item. - Image attributes are written in a fixed order. - A footnote definition is no longer read as a link definition, link urls keep balanced parentheses, and image references (`![alt][]`) resolve. - Fences close only with the character that opened them, at least as many times. - An item's indented rules stay in the item, and an unindented rule or heading ends the list. - Setext headings take every line of their paragraph. - Blockquotes keep indented code as code, and a heading or quote inside a quote stays in it. - Letter and Roman numeral lists need two items in sequence. - A newer copy of the library keeps the config changes AddOns made to the older one. ### Added - Nested lists, task lists, GFM tables, `~~strikethrough~~`, bare url links, footnotes, `~~~` fences, shortcut references, and backslash line breaks. - Alerts, definition lists, highlight, superscript and subscript, and heading ids, from other Markdown flavors; atlases, shortcodes, and game link tooltips for WoW. - `:ToHTML(text, settings)` and `:New(settings)`, so an AddOn's settings don't change the shared config.

releases.notes:
## 1.0.5

- The `hard_breaks` setting, for text typed as in chat, such as notes: every line break in a paragraph is
  shown, and a blank line after a paragraph is an empty line, as in a GitHub comment. It's off by default,
  so other AddOns' text renders as before.

## 1.0.4 Syntax from other Markdown flavors (not in CommonMark or GFM, but what other renderers use): - GitHub's alerts: a quote starting `[!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]`, or `[!CAUTION]` shows an icon and a colored title, then its text. - Definition lists: a term line, then `: definition` lines. - `==Highlight==`, shown in a color, and `x^2^` / `H~2~O`, shown with Unicode superscript and subscript characters (`script_glyphs`). - Heading ids: `## Setup {#setup}` hides the id, and `:GetHeadings(text)` lists every heading's level, text, and id, for a table of contents or for handling `[links](#setup)`. WoW extensions: - Atlases: `![](atlas:name)` or `![](atlas:name 32x32)` is shown in the line. - Shortcodes: `:check:`, `:x:`, `:question:`, `:warning:`, `:gold:`, `:silver:`, `:copper:`, `:tank:`, `:healer:`, and `:dps:` become icons. Add your own as config keys, like `[":myicon:"]`. - `:ShowLinkTooltip(owner, link)` and `:HideLinkTooltip()` show the game's tooltip for links such as `[Fireball](spell:133)` from a frame's hyperlink scripts. - Game icons: `![](spell:133)`, `![](item:6948 20x20)`, and the same for currencies and achievements show that thing's icon inside the line. - Inline textures: `![](Interface\ICONS\X 16x16 inline)` is shown inside the line instead of as a block. If rendering fails, `:ToHTML()` reports the error through WoW's error handler and returns the text as plain paragraphs, instead of raising the error into the AddOn showing it. `\^`, `\=`, and `\:` are backslash escapes, for text these would otherwise change. Faster: - Rendering is several times faster: a 51 KB news page went from about 450 ms to about 60 ms. Showing a document again with the same settings takes no time at all, since recent renders are kept (changing any setting renders it again). Blockquotes look like they do in other renderers: left-aligned gray text with a bar at the start of each line (`blockquote_bar`), instead of centered yellow text in quote marks between two rules. A quote inside a quote adds its own bar, and alerts have a bar in their kind's color (`admonition_note_bar` and so on). SimpleHTML can't put a bar on the wrapped part of a long line. Level 4 to 6 headings are told apart from level 3 (SimpleHTML has no smaller heading styles): they're lines at text size, level 4 in the strong color, level 5 in the strong_em color, and level 6 in gray. The `h4`, `h5`, and `h6` settings (with `h4_style` and so on) change them; `h4 = "

"`, `["/h4"] = "


"`, and `h4_style = false` show level 4 as level 3 again. Also: - A loose list item's later paragraphs and code start indented under the item's text. - `***both***` has a color of its own (`strong_em`), instead of em's color inside strong's. - A blank line ends a blockquote, so two quotes (or alerts) with a blank line between them are two blocks. A line of just `>` still continues a quote.

## 1.0.3 New Markdown support: - Nested lists. Each level is indented further, and `list_marker_2`, `list_marker_3`, and so on can give each level its own marker. - Task lists: `- [ ]` and `- [x]` show an empty box or a check mark. - Tables. SimpleHTML can't lay out columns, so each row is a line of cells between separators, with the header row colored. - `~~Strikethrough~~`, shown dimmed. - Bare `https://` and `www.` addresses become links. - Footnotes: `[^id]` shows a number, and the notes (`[^id]: text`) are listed at the end of the document. - `~~~` code fences, and fences of four or more backticks, which can hold a ``` line. - Shortcut references (`[id]`) and image references (`![alt][]`, `![alt]`). - A backslash at the end of a line breaks it, like two trailing spaces. Settings without changing other AddOns' text: - `:ToHTML(text, settings)` applies settings to that call only, and `:New(settings)` makes a renderer with its own settings. Changing the library's `config` table changes the text of every AddOn that uses it. - The AceGUI widget's settings now apply only to the widget. - When a newer copy of the library loads, the config changes AddOns made to the older copy are kept. They were dropped. Bug fixes: - A closing tag with no opening tag (``), a tag left open, or `
` without a slash no longer makes SimpleHTML show the whole document as raw text. - Blockquote lines are joined with a space instead of run together, and a blank `>` line no longer adds a `"`. - `snake_case_names` aren't emphasized, `#hashtag` isn't a heading, and `**x**` is strong. - A `|` in code is shown as itself instead of starting a UI escape sequence. - The `^` that ends a list is no longer shown. - Lists are numbered correctly when an item spans several lines, and an item's indented paragraphs, code, and rules stay in the item. Ordered items keep the `)` or `.` typed after their number. - A bullet list, or one starting at 1, can start right after a paragraph line. An unindented rule or heading ends a list. - "A. Lincoln was president." and "I. M. Pei" aren't lists: a letter or Roman numeral list needs at least two items in sequence. - A footnote definition no longer turns into a broken link definition that eats the note's first word. - Link urls keep balanced parentheses, as in `(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lua_(programming_language))`, and backslash escapes work in link definitions' urls. - A setext heading (text underlined with `===` or `---`) takes every line of its paragraph. - Blockquotes keep code indented in them as code, and a heading or quote inside a quote stays in it instead of leaving a stray `"` on a line of its own. Also new: `Showcase.lua`, an in-game tour of everything the library renders (enable it in `LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown.xml`, then type `/lshm`), and tests that run on every push and before each release.

## 1.0.2 Bug fixes. Each of these could leave a document mangled, or make SimpleHTML show the whole document as raw text. - An unclosed code fence no longer turns later documents into code blocks, including documents from other AddOns, since the library object is shared. - A `<` that doesn't start a tag (`x`. HTML inside a code fence stays code. - Blocks are never nested: loose list items, code in list items, and headings or images inside another block become a flat run of blocks. - Numeric character references and common named entities (Latin-1, dashes, curly quotes, arrows, and so on) are decoded to the character. Any other entity is shown literally.

## 1.0.1

First release. LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown is a fork of [LibMarkdown-1.0](https://github.com/endurantgames/WoW-LibMarkdown) by Oraibi-MoonGuard, which is no longer maintained, starting from its last version, minor 9. It registers under its own LibStub name, `LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown-1.0`, so it never collides with copies of LibMarkdown that other AddOns still embed.

- `:ToHTML()` accepts a table of strings, as documented; LibMarkdown always printed an error.
- Reference links and images, `<user@example.org>` autolinks, and a code fence on the last line no longer error.
- Roman numeral lists (`i.`, `ii.`) are recognized as Roman numerals.
- The AceGUI widget is `SimpleHTMLMarkdown_Description`, and it only registers when `AceGUI-3.0` is loaded.

See [Changes from LibMarkdown](https://github.com/Twintop/LibSimpleHTMLMarkdown#changes-from-libmarkdown) for every rename and fix.
